newsitem.title: FINLAND: INSTRUMENTARIUM SEES GOOD SALES TREND.
newsitem.headline: INSTRUMENTARIUM SEES GOOD SALES TREND.

text.p: Finnish medical equipment maker Instrumentarium said in its eight-month interim statement on Friday it expected its net sales to continue developing favourably this year.
Eight-month net sales rose to 1.50 billion markka from 1.35 billion and the profit before extraordinary items rose to 183 million markka from 165 million.
"Instrumentarium group's net sales are estimated to continue to develop favourably during the year 1996," it said.

It said the outlook for the anaesthesia and critical care business was better than last year but noted that sales growth in the final four months of the year has not normally been as strong as in the first eiqht months.
On the other hand, "demand for medical equipment and supplies is expected to strengthen towards the year end," it said.
Demand for optical retail and distribution of consumer and commercial products remains stable for the rest of the year, it said.
